input.prompt: Match the reference image's palette, ornament and painting style closely, recomposed as a portrait frame. Painted like a background from an early 1930s American theatrical cartoon short (an original scene, not any existing studio, film or character): hand-inked black outlines with slight wobble, gouache and watercolour painting with visible brush texture, a warm early three-strip Technicolor print palette of deep crimson, vermilion, teal-green, burnished gold and warm cream, soft painted light and shadow, a faint film grain. Scene: the front of a 1930s art deco picture palace at night seen straight on, perfectly symmetrical: the marquee canopy is edged with rows of round glowing bulbs and chrome and red enamel deco trim; its face is ONE large reader board of warm amber backlit glass crossed by FOUR long, evenly spaced horizontal rows of thin dark letter rails, every row completely empty; a tall vertical blade sign rising above the canopy with blank lit panels; a curved glass ticket booth and brass doors under the canopy; wet pavement reflecting the lights; a deep teal night sky with soft clouds. Portrait framing: the blade sign rises through the top 28%, the reader board spans the middle 86% of the width and sits between 32% and 68% of the height, the ticket booth and doors below it. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing.
